name: Stripes (1981)
description: AirCal's scheme from its 1981 renaming until the 1987 merger into American: a white aircraft with a cheatline of four bands, yellow, orange, red and a dark aubergine, top to bottom. Ahead of the wing the bands sit low, the windows in the yellow and orange, and they run on round the nose, the aubergine reaching the nose tip. Behind the forward titles the whole stack steps up about half a meter in a smooth slanted S, each band a little behind the one under it, so aft of the step the windows are in the red. Ahead of the tail one straight diagonal, about 36 degrees, cuts the bands off. Aft of it the body is aubergine from just above the windows' foot to the crown, back over the tail cone, and on the fin the same line runs on up to the trailing edge: aft of it the fin is banded level in yellow, orange, red and a little aubergine at the root, the yellow's top rounding level into the trailing edge. 'AIRCAL' in aubergine ahead of the step over the windows and on the fin's white, parallel to the diagonal. Bare metal wings; bare metal engines on the 737-200s, white on the MD-80s.

sources.title: 2-10-85 Los Angeles N463GB (CC BY 2.0, Pete Macklin)
sources.note: 737-200 N463GB, right side, Los Angeles, 2 October 1985: the scheme on the -200 (the step just behind the forward door, the fin's rounded yellow corner), bare metal nacelles, the colors.

sources.title: 6-10-85 Los Angeles N467GB (CC BY 2.0, Pete Macklin)
sources.note: 737-200 N467GB, left side from above, Los Angeles, 6 October 1985: the left side's title and step on the -200, the aubergine wedge and tail cone.

sources.title: AirCal Boeing 737-200 N466AC (CC BY-SA 3.0, Eduard Marmet)

sources.title: AirCal MD-82; N478AC (CC BY-SA 2.0, Aero Icarus)
sources.note: MD-82 N478AC, left side, side-on, undated (in AirCal's paint, so 1985-87): the MD-80's band heights, step, diagonal, fin bands and titles measured on it against shapes/MD82.json (by the crown, the first window, the forward door, the nose and the tail cone; the camera about 3.5 degrees below). sources.note: MD-81 N475AC landing, left side, 14 July 1984, in even light: the MD-80 fin's bands top to bottom (yellow under the tailplane, orange, red, a deep aubergine at the root) where N478AC's fin is half in shadow.

notes: Measured 2026-11-24 for Skyarium's ghost flights, on the 737-300 (shapes/B733.json), which stands in for AirCal's 737-200s; the MD-80s have their own paint in types.MD82. AirCal's code OC is keyed with its founding year (OC1967). The edges are lines in meters, not traced points: each band edge is a constant height (737: ahead of the step 0.72, 0.47, 0.22, -0.27 and -0.765 m from the cabin's centerline, aft of it 0.52 m higher), each step a cosine-eased S 1.36 m long, each edge's step a little behind the one under it (as on N308AC, where the yellow nearly pinches out in the step), and one straight diagonal at 35.7 degrees runs from the stack's foot (rounded into it, radius 1.2 m) up the body and the fin to the trailing edge, its top rounding level into the trailing edge. Aft of it the body is aubergine down to 0.71 m (rounded where it meets the diagonal, radius 1.5 m). The fin's bands are level (4.19, 3.40 and 2.08 m). Converted to the shape and thinned to within 3 mm. Heights good to about 0.05 m, positions along the body to about 0.2 m on the 737 and 0.3 m on the MD-80. Uncertain: the MD-80 fin's band heights (N478AC's fin top is in the tailplane's shadow and the aubergine there reads as shadow; checked on MD-81 N475AC); where the aubergine's lower edge meets the tail cone (under the tailplane on every photo); the 737's tailplane color (drawn bare metal); the 737-300s' white nacelles (drawn bare metal, as on the 737-200s the broadcast paints); the small registration over the aft windows is left out. The date the merger ended the scheme is taken as July 1987; ex-AirCal jets flew on in this paint with American titles for a while after.

MD82.note: Measured on MD-82 N478AC: the same design on the MD-80's outline. The bands sit about 0.1 m lower against the centerline (the windows do too), the step is ahead of the wing at 11-14 m, and the diagonal meets the fin's trailing edge right under the tailplane, so the yellow is a small corner there. White nacelles and pylons, white tailplane.
